text.p: These are the leading stories in Serbian and Montenegrin papers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
- S E R B I A -
NASA BORBA
- Serbian draft law on ownership transformation does not obligate companies to privatise. Parliament to pass the bill at its session June 30, implementation from end of October.

- The United States will continue to monitor all legal proceedings against independent media in Serbia, case against Nasa Borba must be public, U.S. government says in statement through embassy in Belgrade.
- Doctors and nurses block several downtown streets in Belgrade on 39th day of strikes over late wages.
- U.S. agency for renewal and development to invest $3.7 million in the Brcko region in Bosnia this year. Memorandum of understanding signed by the two sides on Thursday.
- The door to Croatia's return to Europe closed if it does not allow Serbs to return, says U.S. Ambassador to Croatia Peter Galbraith during visit to Knin region.
- A total of 75,249 Bosnian refugees registered in Yugoslavia for local elections in Bosnia on September 13-14.
- New fixed import duties for agricultural and food products, payable in dinars per unit, to prevent tax evasion and reduce the agriculture sector's trade deficit.
- There can be no transformation of banks with socialist-style enterprises, says National Bank of Yugoslavia Deputy Governor Bozidar Gazivoda.

- Consistent implementation of central bank regulations would mean 99 banks would lose permits, warns the Association of Yugoslav Banks. Not a single state bank among seven financial institutions that meet strict criteria.
- There can be no rehabilitation of banks without International Monetary Fund and World Bank participation, says Economics Institute Director Vera Leko.
POLITIKA
- "Our goal is a powerful, economically strong and democratically developed country," says Yugoslav President Zoran Lilic at the end of his four-year mandate.
- The bulk of social and state capital will go to those who created it, and not to a narrow circle of privileged and economically powerful, says Serbian Prime Minister Mirko Marjanovic.
- Yugoslavia, Italy sign agreement abolishing visas for business travel and diplomats during Yugoslav Foreign Minister Milan Milutinovic's visit to Rome.

- Yugoslavia, Romania cooperate on exploitation of Djerdap hydroelectric power plant. Seventh 27-megawatt block to be built, revitalisation of existing six to raise Djedrap 1 power from 175 to 190 megawatts.

- Serbian Privatisation Minister Milan Beko says 80 percent of companies expected to be privatised in the next two years. Total socially- and state-owned capital in Serbia evaluated at 100 billion German Marks.
- Party of Democratic Action of Sandzak leader Sulejman Ugljanin denies allegations of plans to proclaim the majority Moslem region's autonomy.
- M O N T E N E G R O -
POBJEDA

- Montenegrin President Momir Bulatovic in address to parliament accuses the government of abetting crime. In separate speeches Deputy Prime Minister Miodrag Vukovic, Interior Minister Filip Vujanovic, Justice Minister Dusko Lalicevic and Culture Minister Goran Rakocevic said Bulatovic did not have any evidence for his allegations.
- Three republican funds -- Social Insurance, Unemployment and Development -- privatise six more companies. Total value of six companies privatised so far is 17.8 million German marks.
MONITOR

- On the excuse of stopping illegal crossing of Montenegrin borders, the Yugoslav Navy fired at a convoy loaded with cigarettes in "re-export business". Strict "customs controls" recently established between Serbia and Montenegro.

- Incidents between the navy and Montenegrin police are a logical consequence of flexing muscles on Montenegro. The navy plans to remove Montenegrin resistance to centralisation of the federation and to economically ruin Montenegro in order to stop Montenegrin self-financing, commenatry.
- Parliament speaker Svetozar Marovic is the most popular figure in DPS and has chances of winning against Momir Bulatovic in party nomination for republican president, according to internal polls.

- It is Milosevic's deception that he can keep Montenegro in colonial subservience by the "one man, one vote principle. Because of that principle Slovenia, Croatia, Macedonia and Bosnia-Herzegovina fled from Serbia. Why should Montenegro be drawn to Serbia when it could be in a better economic position than in 1989 after few years of independence, says Dragan Veselinov in a news analysis. -- Belgrade newsroom +381 11 222 4305
